cards.hook: The honeymoon ends mid-air — and somewhere over the Pacific, a new chapter quietly begins.

cards.headline: The last perfect days
cards.body: This week opened in the warmth of French Polynesia and closed on a plane home. Between those two points: 4am work calls from Tahaa, a lavish dinner with drinks that felt entirely worth it, and a flight back to SF carrying something new — not just memories, but the quiet weight of what comes next.
cards.quote: Really really great day. So thankful to be here. More sun burnt than I want to be but it feels like a big dose of vitamin D did me good.
cards.image_hint: French Polynesia lagoon at golden hour

moments.title: The permission you gave yourself
moments.body: Something shifted on this day — not dramatically, but meaningfully. You wrote that even though you love Gremly, you needed to step back and just enjoy Dave on a once-in-a-lifetime vacation. That sentence wasn't a complaint. It was a choice. And the days that followed were lighter for it.
moments.image_hint: Bora Bora overwater bungalow at dusk

moments.title: Boarding with a list and a feeling
moments.body: Anxious and sad to be leaving, but grateful — and already building the mental architecture of return. The list you wrote mid-boarding (Gremly, work, myself, Dave) tells its own story about where your mind goes first. But you wrote it, which means you're watching yourself. That's not nothing.

threads.name: Surrogacy & Family Planning
threads.shift_label: First signal of a new chapter
threads.detail: A single todo — 'Surrogacy Agencies Research' — created on March 15, the last day in Bora Bora, without fanfare or journal explanation.

threads.name: Sobriety & Alcohol-Free Streak
threads.detail: On March 21, a lavish dinner with drinks — and unlike the Valentine's slip in February, the journal entry reads simply: 'it was worth it.'

threads.name: Running & Half Marathon Training
threads.detail: March 22 was both race day and the return flight from Tahiti. Only one run was logged all week (March 18 in Tahaa). No journal entry mentions the race.

threads.name: Mental Wellbeing & Negative Thought Management
threads.detail: Four consecutive completions from March 10–13, the longest run since the habit started, with gratitude language flooding every journal entry during the streak.

threads.name: Partnership with Dave
threads.detail: Dave appears in all four journal entries this week — floaties, tennis on March 14, early morning islands — and the intimacy entry on March 17 is the most candid the journals have been.

threads.name: App Development & Launch
threads.detail: Work maps concept introduced on March 19 from Tahaa — described as 'something for a long long time in the future but could be huge for B2B.'

spotlight.title: Two health habits, running in opposite directions
spotlight.takeaway: Your mind has never been clearer. Your sobriety commitment has almost entirely dissolved. Both live in the same domain — and the journals never once name the gap.
spotlight.evidence_trail: Negative thought management hit a 4-day consecutive streak (March 10–13) — the best run since the habit began, at 33% cumulative. Sobriety logged only 1 completion across the entire week (March 9), sitting at 14% overall across 21 days. Multiple detailed journal entries from Bora Bora and Tahaa this week — not one mentions alcohol. The person managing their mind beautifully was also quietly not managing the commitment made to their body.

research_context.title: Why this happens
research_context.body: Baumeister's ego depletion research suggests self-control draws from a shared resource pool. When emotional regulation is working well (gratitude practice, positive reframing), willpower for behavioral commitments like sobriety may quietly deplete — especially in high-reward environments.

mini_discoveries.title: The todo that appeared mid-honeymoon
mini_discoveries.detail: 'Surrogacy Agencies Research' was created March 15 in Bora Bora — no journal entry explains it, no prior thread anticipates it.

mini_discoveries.title: Work walked in through the side door
mini_discoveries.detail: 4am calls from Tahaa on March 17 — still on honeymoon, already back on client obligations, and notably: 'I'm happy to be doing it from a beautiful island.'

primary.title: Decide what the sobriety commitment means now
primary.body: The March 21 dinner was guilt-free — 'it was worth it' — which is different from February's Valentine's slip. That shift matters. Before SF resets everything, it's worth asking: is this commitment still yours, or has it quietly become something you're carrying out of inertia? Either answer is valid. But choosing consciously is better than drifting.

secondary.title: Let the half marathon have a moment
secondary.body: Race day passed on March 22 without a single journal word. Whether you ran it, deferred it, or simply let it go — it deserves a sentence. Goals that disappear in silence tend to leave residue.

secondary.title: Don't rush the surrogacy todo
secondary.body: It appeared mid-honeymoon, spontaneously. That timing is meaningful. Give it space before it becomes a project — some things are better held loosely at first.

cards.headline: 12 items need attention
cards.body: Most of these were created before the honeymoon and held patiently while you were away. Now that you're back, a quick pass will clear the slate.

cards.intro: Sunday lands you back in SF — Bella, habits, and a 'new lease on life' all waiting. Two things on March 22 deserve attention before the week begins in earnest.

highlights.title: Half Marathon
highlights.prep_nudge: Clarify whether this was run, deferred, or missed — then close the loop in your journal.
highlights.context: Race day and return flight are both March 22. The data strongly suggests the race was not run.

highlights.title: Flight to San Francisco
highlights.prep_nudge: You wrote 'good habits and a focused mind' — consider writing down what that actually means before you land.
highlights.context: The honeymoon officially ends here. You called it 'a new lease on life in SF.'

busy_day_warnings.detail: Long travel day from Tahiti plus potential race day conflict — give yourself grace on arrival.
